note: Generated from data/tables/flora.json yields by tools/gen_gathered_items.py. Numbers start at 1000 and are append-only: re-running only adds new yields. Each yield becomes a plain material until food, herb and potion systems give them effects. Numbers 1008 and 1083 are retired (bark and leaves became core items 13 and 14); never reuse them.

acorns.name: Acorns
acorns.description: Oak nuts, bitter raw. Soaked and mashed they make a poor but filling food.

aloe_gel.name: Aloe gel
aloe_gel.description: Cool clear gel from a split aloe leaf. Soothes burns and sun-reddened skin.

amadou.name: Amadou
amadou.description: Soft felt peeled from a tinder fungus. Dried, it takes a spark and holds an ember.

angelica_roots.name: Angelica roots
angelica_roots.description: A thick aromatic root of angelica. Chewed or steeped as a warming remedy.

angelica_stems.name: Angelica stems
angelica_stems.description: Hollow green stems of angelica, sweet and sharp. Eaten fresh or candied.

arnica_flowers.name: Arnica flowers
arnica_flowers.description: Bright yellow mountain daisies. Their salve eases bruises; never eat them.

banana_leaves.name: Banana leaves
banana_leaves.description: Broad glossy leaves of the wild banana. Good for wrapping food and shelter roofs.

bananas.name: Bananas
bananas.description: Short sweet wild bananas, full of seeds. Ripe ones are soft and yellow.

bedding.name: Bedding
bedding.description: Soft dry stuff to lie on. A bed is stuffed with it.

beechnuts.name: Beechnuts
beechnuts.description: Small three-sided beech nuts in prickly husks. Eaten roasted or pressed for oil.

belladonna_berries.name: Belladonna berries
belladonna_berries.description: Shiny black berries of deadly nightshade. Poisonous: do not eat.

belladonna_leaves.name: Belladonna leaves
belladonna_leaves.description: Dull green leaves of deadly nightshade. Poisonous: a healer's herb at best.

birch_bark.name: Birch bark
birch_bark.description: Papery white bark that peels in sheets. Burns even when damp; useful as tinder or for containers.

blackberries.name: Blackberries
blackberries.description: Dark juicy brambles berries, sweet when fully black. Eaten fresh or cooked.

blueberries.name: Blueberries
blueberries.description: Small blue berries from low bushes. Sweet, and they stain the fingers.

brinebells.name: Brinebells
brinebells.description: Salt-loving shore flowers that ring like little bells. Chewed, they taste of the sea.

burdock_roots.name: Burdock roots
burdock_roots.description: A long dark taproot, earthy and sweet when cooked. Dug from disturbed ground.

burrs.name: Burrs
burrs.description: Hooked seed heads of burdock that cling to cloth and fur. Pests, and a kind of fastener.

cactus_pads.name: Cactus pads
cactus_pads.description: Flat fleshy cactus pads, spines still on. Peeled and cooked they make food and water.

chamomile_flowers.name: Chamomile flowers
chamomile_flowers.description: Small white daisies with yellow centres. A calming tea.

chanterelles.name: Chanterelles
chanterelles.description: Golden funnel-shaped mushrooms with a fruity smell. A good find in the woods.

charcoal_wood.name: Charcoal wood
charcoal_wood.description: Alder wood fit for burning down to charcoal. Hotter and cleaner than a wood fire.

cherries.name: Cherries
cherries.description: Small dark wild cherries, tart. Eaten fresh, or pitted and cooked.

cherry_wood.name: Cherry wood
cherry_wood.description: Reddish close-grained wood of the wild cherry. Takes a polish; makes fine small work.

chestnuts.name: Chestnuts
chestnuts.description: Glossy brown nuts in spiny husks. Roasted, they are sweet and starchy.

cinderfoot_caps.name: Cinderfoot caps
cinderfoot_caps.description: Rust-orange mushroom caps with dark gills, found where old fires burned. Not for eating until identified.

cloudberries.name: Cloudberries
cloudberries.description: Amber northern berries on low bogs. Rare, tart and prized.

coconuts.name: Coconuts
coconuts.description: A heavy husked nut with sweet water inside. Crack it open to drink.

comfrey_leaves.name: Comfrey leaves
comfrey_leaves.description: Rough hairy leaves of comfrey. Bruised and bound on sprains as a poultice.

comfrey_roots.name: Comfrey roots
comfrey_roots.description: A thick black root of comfrey, mucky and slimy inside. Used for poultices; not for eating.

crab_apples.name: Crab apples
crab_apples.description: Hard sour little apples. Cooked down with honey they are good.

cranberries.name: Cranberries
cranberries.description: Tart red berries of the bog. They keep a long time.

crowberries.name: Crowberries
crowberries.description: Black berries of low moorland shrubs. Watery and mild; better than nothing.

dandelion_flowers.name: Dandelion flowers
dandelion_flowers.description: Bright yellow flower heads. Fried or steeped for tea.

dandelion_leaves.name: Dandelion leaves
dandelion_leaves.description: Bitter toothed leaves. Eaten as a spring salad or boiled.

dandelion_roots.name: Dandelion roots
dandelion_roots.description: A long pale taproot, bitter. Roasted and ground as a coffee, or boiled.

dates.name: Dates
dates.description: Sticky sweet dates from a date palm. They keep well and travel well.

drakethorn_berries.name: Drakethorn berries
drakethorn_berries.description: Dark red berries on a thorny shrub said to grow where drakes have lain. Handle with care until identified.

duskmallow_flowers.name: Duskmallow flowers
duskmallow_flowers.description: Soft violet blooms that open at dusk. Their scent is calming.

duskmallow_roots.name: Duskmallow roots
duskmallow_roots.description: Pale roots of duskmallow, slimy when boiled. Soothes a sore throat.

dye.name: Dye
dye.description: A pot of plant colour pressed from flowers and roots. Stains cloth and wood.

echo_moss.name: Echo moss
echo_moss.description: Springy grey-green moss that seems to muffle sound around it. Grows in damp hollows.

elderberries.name: Elderberries
elderberries.description: Dark purple berries in drooping clusters. Cooked, they are good; raw they upset the stomach.

elderflowers.name: Elderflowers
elderflowers.description: Creamy lacy flower sprays with a sweet musky smell. Steeped as a cordial.

emberroots.name: Emberroots
emberroots.description: Red-brown roots that stay warm to the touch. Said to be good fuel and a hot spice.

everember_needles.name: Everember needles
everember_needles.description: Needles of the everember tree, dark green and resinous. They smoulder rather than burn.

everember_sap.name: Everember sap
everember_sap.description: A sticky amber sap that smells of warm spice. Burns slowly.

everember_wood.name: Everember wood
everember_wood.description: Dense dark wood of the everember, slow to burn and warm to hold.

feverfew.name: Feverfew
feverfew.description: Small daisy-like flowers with bitter leaves. A headache remedy.

fibre.name: Fibre
fibre.description: Tough plant strands. Twisted into twine.

fiddleheads.name: Fiddleheads
fiddleheads.description: Tightly curled young fern fronds. Cooked, they taste green and nutty.

fine_wood.name: Fine wood
fine_wood.description: Well-grown timber chosen for its grain. Makes quality lumber and furniture.

fly_agaric_caps.name: Fly agaric caps
fly_agaric_caps.description: Bright red caps with white flecks. Poisonous: do not eat.

fodder.name: Fodder
fodder.description: Coarse leaves and twigs that animals will eat. No good for people.

food.name: Food
food.description: Plain edible things gathered in the wild. Eat to stay on your feet.

foxglove_leaves.name: Foxglove leaves
foxglove_leaves.description: Soft downy leaves of foxglove. Poisonous: a heart medicine in the right hands.

frostglass_petals.name: Frostglass petals
frostglass_petals.description: Clear glassy petals of an orchid that grows on the frozen slopes. Brittle and cold to touch.

gloaming_star.name: Gloaming star
gloaming_star.description: A pale star-shaped flower that glows faintly at dusk. Picked, it fades by morning.

gloomthistle_down.name: Gloomthistle down
gloomthistle_down.description: Dark grey thistle fluff, soft and light. Fills pillows and burns quick.

gloomthistle_heads.name: Gloomthistle heads
gloomthistle_heads.description: Spiny dark thistle heads. Handle with gloves.

greens.name: Greens
greens.description: Mixed wild leaves, nettle and the like. Boiled they are a plain green food.

gum.name: Gum
gum.description: Sticky tree gum, hardened in lumps. Chewed, or used as glue.

hagwillow_bark.name: Hagwillow bark
hagwillow_bark.description: Grey twisted bark of the hag willow, bitter. Steeped it eases aches.

hagwillow_withies.name: Hagwillow withies
hagwillow_withies.description: Springy shoots of the hag willow. Woven into baskets and fences.

hard_wood.name: Hard wood
hard_wood.description: Heavy dense wood, slow to cut. Makes strong tool handles and posts.

hardwood.name: Hardwood
hardwood.description: Heavy timber from broadleaf trees such as oak and beech. Strong, and slow to burn.

haws.name: Haws
haws.description: Small red berries of the hawthorn, mealy and mild. Cooked into jelly.

hawthorn_blossom.name: Hawthorn blossom
hawthorn_blossom.description: White spring blossom of the hawthorn, sweet and faintly rank. A mild heart tonic.

hazelnuts.name: Hazelnuts
hazelnuts.description: Round hard-shelled nuts. Crack and eat; they keep well.

hearthwood_logs.name: Hearthwood logs
hearthwood_logs.description: Heavy logs of the hearthwood tree, said to burn all night and never spit.

heartroots.name: Heartroots
heartroots.description: Red knotted roots shaped like fists. A hardy food and a warming remedy.

henbane_leaves.name: Henbane leaves
henbane_leaves.description: Sticky hairy leaves of henbane. Poisonous: do not eat.

henbane_seeds.name: Henbane seeds
henbane_seeds.description: Tiny grey seeds from a henbane pod. Poisonous: do not eat.

herbs.name: Herbs
herbs.description: A bundle of mixed wild herbs. Flavours food.

honey_flowers.name: Honey flowers
honey_flowers.description: Heather flowers heavy with nectar. Bees love them; so does a good honey.

honeyspindle_nectar.name: Honeyspindle nectar
honeyspindle_nectar.description: A sweet golden nectar drained from honeyspindle flowers. Sweetens any dish.

honeyspindle_pods.name: Honeyspindle pods
honeyspindle_pods.description: Slim pods of the honeyspindle, full of sweet seed. Good to chew.

hushfern_fronds.name: Hushfern fronds
hushfern_fronds.description: Soft grey fronds that deaden footfalls. Poisonous: do not eat.

juniper_berries.name: Juniper berries
juniper_berries.description: Dark blue aromatic berries. Flavour meats and ferment drinks.

kindling.name: Kindling
kindling.description: Thin dry twigs and shavings that catch quickly. The start of any fire.

lantern_dew.name: Lantern dew
lantern_dew.description: Glowing drops collected from the dewlantern plant. Faintly lights a dark corner.

lavender_flowers.name: Lavender flowers
lavender_flowers.description: Purple flower spikes with a clean scent. Dried they sweeten linen.

lingonberries.name: Lingonberries
lingonberries.description: Small tart red berries. Keep well and cook well.

linseed.name: Linseed
linseed.description: Small shiny brown flax seeds, rich in oil. Eaten or pressed.

lumencap_caps.name: Lumencap caps
lumencap_caps.description: Pale mushroom caps that glow softly in the dark. Not for eating until identified.

marjoram.name: Marjoram
marjoram.description: A sweet herb with oval leaves. Flavours meat and stews.

marrowroots.name: Marrowroots
marrowroots.description: Fat pale roots as thick as a wrist. Cooked, they are soft and filling.

meadowsweet_flowers.name: Meadowsweet flowers
meadowsweet_flowers.description: Frothy cream flowers smelling of honey and almonds. A mild remedy for aches.

mint.name: Mint
mint.description: Fresh green leaves with a cool sharp scent. Flavours food and tea.

mirrorbark_bark.name: Mirrorbark bark
mirrorbark_bark.description: Smooth silver bark that gleams like a mirror in sunlight. Peels in bright sheets.

mirrorbark_wood.name: Mirrorbark wood
mirrorbark_wood.description: Fine pale wood from the mirrorbark tree. Takes a bright polish.

mirrorcap_caps.name: Mirrorcap caps
mirrorcap_caps.description: Shiny silver-grey mushroom caps. Not for eating until identified.

morels.name: Morels
morels.description: Honeycombed brown mushroom caps found in spring. Eaten cooked, never raw.

mournbloom_petals.name: Mournbloom petals
mournbloom_petals.description: Dark petals of the mournbloom, grown over old graves. Not for eating.

mugwort.name: Mugwort
mugwort.description: Grey-green leaves with a bitter smell. A hardy herb, steeped or burned.

nightcrown_blooms.name: Nightcrown blooms
nightcrown_blooms.description: Large pale flowers that open only at night. Scent heavy and sweet.

oil.name: Oil
oil.description: A small jar of pressed plant oil. Cooks, lights lamps and keeps leather supple.

owlpetals.name: Owlpetals
owlpetals.description: Round pale petals marked like eyes. Said to help one see in the dark.

palm_fronds.name: Palm fronds
palm_fronds.description: Long woody fronds. Woven into mats and roofs.

palm_wood.name: Palm wood
palm_wood.description: Fibrous trunk wood of palms. Soft to cut, poor for fuel.

pilgrims_cup_pitchers.name: Pilgrims cup pitchers
pilgrims_cup_pitchers.description: The cup-shaped leaves of the pilgrim's cup, holding rain. Pick one to drink from.

pilgrims_cup_water.name: Pilgrims cup water
pilgrims_cup_water.description: Clear rainwater held in a pilgrim's cup leaf. Safe enough to drink.

pine_tar.name: Pine tar
pine_tar.description: Thick black tar boiled from pine. Seals roofs and soaks wood against rot.

plantain_leaves.name: Plantain leaves
plantain_leaves.description: Broad ribbed leaves of the common plantain. Chewed and applied to stings and cuts.

poles.name: Poles
poles.description: Long straight shoots cut for fencing and frames. Strong and light.

porcini.name: Porcini
porcini.description: Fat brown-capped mushrooms with a thick pale stem. A fine meal.

potash.name: Potash
potash.description: Grey ash of salt-bush, rich in lye. Used for soap and glass.

prickly_pears.name: Prickly pears
prickly_pears.description: Red-purple fruit of the prickly pear, covered in fine spines. Peel before eating.

puffball.name: Puffball
puffball.description: A round white mushroom the size of a head. Sliced and fried; spoils in a day.

quenchbell_heads.name: Quenchbell heads
quenchbell_heads.description: Blue bell-shaped flower heads holding a mouthful of sweet water.

raspberries.name: Raspberries
raspberries.description: Soft red berries that crumble when picked. Sweet when fully ripe.

raspberry_leaves.name: Raspberry leaves
raspberry_leaves.description: Toothed leaves of the raspberry cane. Steeped as a soothing tea.

reed_stems.name: Reed stems
reed_stems.description: Long hollow stems of reed. Woven or bundled.

resin.name: Resin
resin.description: Sticky sap from conifers, hardened into amber lumps. Burns hot, seals wood, and sticks things.

rimecap_caps.name: Rimecap caps
rimecap_caps.description: Frost-pale mushroom caps that grow on cold north slopes. Not for eating until identified.

riverbraid_stems.name: Riverbraid stems
riverbraid_stems.description: Long flexible stems of a river plant, easily plaited into rope and baskets.

rose_hips.name: Rose hips
rose_hips.description: Bright red seed pods of the wild rose. Tart and full of seeds; boiled into syrup.

rose_petals.name: Rose petals
rose_petals.description: Soft pink wild rose petals. Scent a room or steep in water.

rosemary.name: Rosemary
rosemary.description: A woody herb with narrow needle-like leaves and a strong resinous scent.

rowan_berries.name: Rowan berries
rowan_berries.description: Bright orange-red berries in clusters. Bitter raw; fine cooked into jelly.

sage.name: Sage
sage.description: Soft grey-green leaves with a musky scent. Flavours meat and a remedy for sore throats.

samphire.name: Samphire
samphire.description: Crisp salty green shoots of the shore. Eaten fresh, or pickled.

sap.name: Sap
sap.description: Sweet watery sap tapped from a tree. Boils down to syrup.

sea_buckthorn_berries.name: Sea buckthorn berries
sea_buckthorn_berries.description: Bright orange berries on thorny shore bushes. Sour and oily, rich in vitamins.

seeds.name: Seeds
seeds.description: A handful of plant seeds. Eaten, or sown in a patch.

sevenyear_blossoms.name: Sevenyear blossoms
sevenyear_blossoms.description: Rare white lily blooms, they flower once in seven years. Treasured.

sevenyear_bulbs.name: Sevenyear bulbs
sevenyear_bulbs.description: A pale bulb of the sevenyear lily. Said to wait years for its season.

sleetberries.name: Sleetberries
sleetberries.description: Small blue-white berries that ripen after the first frost. Sharp and sweet.

sloes.name: Sloes
sloes.description: Small hard blue-black plums of the blackthorn. Very sour; ripe after frost.

softwood.name: Softwood
softwood.description: Light timber from pine, spruce and fir. Easy to work, fast to burn.

sorrel_leaves.name: Sorrel leaves
sorrel_leaves.description: Sharp lemony arrow-shaped leaves. Eaten fresh or cooked into soup.

spines.name: Spines
spines.description: Long sharp cactus spines. Used as needles and pins.

st_johns_wort.name: St johns wort
st_johns_wort.description: Yellow star flowers with dotted leaves. Steeped for a gentle remedy.

staunchmoss.name: Staunchmoss
staunchmoss.description: Soft spongy moss that stops bleeding when packed on a wound.

stillwater_petals.name: Stillwater petals
stillwater_petals.description: Pale petals of the stillwater lotus. Float on calm pools.

stillwater_seeds.name: Stillwater seeds
stillwater_seeds.description: Round seeds of the stillwater lotus. Eaten roasted; keep well.

stormreed_stalks.name: Stormreed stalks
stormreed_stalks.description: Tough hollow stalks of a reed that sings in a gale. Strong and flexible.

straw.name: Straw
straw.description: Dry grass stalks. Good for bedding and thatch.

strawberries.name: Strawberries
strawberries.description: Small sweet red wild strawberries. Better than any garden berry.

stuffing.name: Stuffing
stuffing.description: Soft fluff for filling a bed or a pack.

sunberries.name: Sunberries
sunberries.description: Warm golden berries that grow in full sun. Sweet and juicy.

sunsilver_leaves.name: Sunsilver leaves
sunsilver_leaves.description: Silvery leaves of a vine that catch the sun. Said to be a good tonic.

tanglewort_vines.name: Tanglewort vines
tanglewort_vines.description: Long wiry vines that snare ankles. Strong cord when stripped and twisted.

tannin_bark.name: Tannin bark
tannin_bark.description: Bark rich in tannin. Used for tanning hides.

thatch.name: Thatch
thatch.description: Dried grass, reed or bark in bundles. Roofs and walls are made of it.

thorny_canes.name: Thorny canes
thorny_canes.description: Long thorny bramble canes. Used for fencing and snares.

thorny_wood.name: Thorny wood
thorny_wood.description: Hard dark wood of the blackthorn, covered in thorns. Makes tough tool handles.

thyme.name: Thyme
thyme.description: A small tough herb with tiny leaves. A fine flavour for meat and fish.

tidecrown_pearls.name: Tidecrown pearls
tidecrown_pearls.description: Smooth pearly beads that grow on a tidal plant. Pretty and valued.

tideglass_fronds.name: Tideglass fronds
tideglass_fronds.description: Clear glassy sea fronds found at the tide line. Brittle; dry to a salt crust.

timber.name: Timber
timber.description: Rough cut trunk wood for building. Squared up it becomes lumber.

tinder.name: Tinder
tinder.description: Fine dry stuff that takes a spark.

tinder_fungus.name: Tinder fungus
tinder_fungus.description: A woody hoof-shaped fungus. Its inner flesh takes a spark.

truthsage_leaves.name: Truthsage leaves
truthsage_leaves.description: Silver-grey leaves with a clean sharp smell. Said to loosen the tongue.

valerian_roots.name: Valerian roots
valerian_roots.description: Strong-smelling pale roots. Steeped to calm the nerves and help sleep.

walnut_husks.name: Walnut husks
walnut_husks.description: Green-black husks of the walnut. Stain the hands brown; used as dye.

walnuts.name: Walnuts
walnuts.description: Wrinkled walnut kernels in hard shells. Rich and oily; keep well.

wardpine_resin.name: Wardpine resin
wardpine_resin.description: Sweet clean resin of the wardpine, believed to keep ill luck away.

wardpine_wood.name: Wardpine wood
wardpine_wood.description: Straight clean wood of the wardpine, light and strongly scented.

water.name: Water
water.description: Plain water, gathered in a container. Drink it or cook with it.

watercress.name: Watercress
watercress.description: Peppery green leaves from running water. Eaten raw or in soup.

whisperfern_fronds.name: Whisperfern fronds
whisperfern_fronds.description: Long fronds that rustle in still air. Said to hear secrets.

wild_carrot_roots.name: Wild carrot roots
wild_carrot_roots.description: Thin pale roots of wild carrot, tough but sweet. Cooked or chewed raw.

wild_garlic_bulbs.name: Wild garlic bulbs
wild_garlic_bulbs.description: Small white bulbs with a sharp smell. Flavour any dish.

wild_garlic_leaves.name: Wild garlic leaves
wild_garlic_leaves.description: Broad green leaves smelling strongly of garlic. Eaten raw or cooked in spring.

wild_pears.name: Wild pears
wild_pears.description: Small hard pears, gritty and sour. Better cooked.

willow_bark.name: Willow bark
willow_bark.description: Grey-brown bark of willow, bitter. Steeped it eases pain and fever.

wispbloom_heads.name: Wispbloom heads
wispbloom_heads.description: Light seed heads that float away at a breath. Drifts on the wind.

withies.name: Withies
withies.description: Long thin willow shoots. Woven into baskets and hurdles.

witness_bark.name: Witness bark
witness_bark.description: Deep-furrowed bark of the witness tree, said to carry old marks and scars.

witness_leaves.name: Witness leaves
witness_leaves.description: Dark leathery leaves of the old witness tree. Not for eating.

wolfsbane_roots.name: Wolfsbane roots
wolfsbane_roots.description: Dark turnip-like roots of wolfsbane. Poisonous: do not eat.

wood.name: Wood
wood.description: Plain cut branches and trunk wood. Burns, or is worked into tools and frames.

yarrow.name: Yarrow
yarrow.description: Feathery leaves and flat white flower heads. Packed on a wound to slow bleeding.
